importInstructions: In the target Microsoft Sentinel workspace, open Analytics > Import and select this JSON file.
For an ARM deployment, set the workspace parameter to the Log Analytics workspace NAME, not its GUID; deploy to its resource group.
Review all disabled rules, validate the required audit action groups and event samples, tune known maintenance and service accounts, then enable selected rules.
Do not enable the loginmanager/dbmanager rule for Managed Instance; it is deliberately Azure SQL Database-only.
designNotes: The original fourteen use cases are preserved, but their KQL is rewritten for MI scoping, robust identifiers, actor/target mappings, explicit success filtering, and short operational schedules.

Individual failure rules produce one summary alert per run. Threshold rules retain the source condition of more than five failures per ten minutes and group by resource to avoid cross-instance mixing.
Threshold rules exclude missing account/IP group keys instead of treating placeholder values as identities. Individual failure rules still retain those events.

Only failed-login events for AzureSQLConnectivityChecker with a private IPv4 source are excluded as the documented internal checker signature. Other failures are not automatically classified as benign.

Role-change patterns accept ALTER ROLE, ALTER SERVER ROLE, and legacy role-member procedures. Legacy procedure parsing supports positional or canonically ordered named literal arguments, not variables, reordered named arguments, or dynamic SQL.
Five- and ten-minute query periods match their schedules to avoid deliberate rolling-window duplicate alerts. Validate ingestion latency; events arriving after their event-time window may be missed.

Existing source overlaps are retained: generic login failures vs threshold failures, and securityadmin removal vs any server-role removal. Enable only the combinations appropriate for your incident workflow.

Native audit events are preferred. BATCH_COMPLETED_GROUP is an alternative for statement coverage but can increase volume, expose sensitive SQL, and produce duplicate observations when combined with native groups.
Scheduled query execution does not verify an actual database deletion or committed transaction. Audit success may describe permission checks; correlate native audit records and database state.

properties.displayName: SQL MI - Database role member added
properties.description: Detects successful ALTER ROLE ADD MEMBER and legacy sp_addrolemember statements, including unquoted and quoted identifiers. Prerequisites: DATABASE_ROLE_MEMBER_CHANGE_GROUP, or BATCH_COMPLETED_GROUP capturing the statement. Source: https://github.com/le0li9ht/Microsoft-Sentinel-Queries/blob/44de43909fee0564e2fb532bf09fe1c2cf4dd5ce/Azure%20SQL/AlteredUserRoleInSQL.kql. All rules import disabled. Review audit coverage, source field quality, thresholds, and maintenance allowlists before enabling. Audit succeeded=true is a reported audit outcome, not independent verification that a transaction committed. Statement-based matching is heuristic and can miss dynamic SQL, comments between tokens, or multiple objects; inspect native audit context. Raw SQL may contain sensitive data; the query retains it for investigation but does not copy it into custom details.
properties.query:
let Identifier = @"(?:\[(?:[^\]]|\]\])+\]|\x22(?:[^\x22]|\x22\x22)+\x22|[A-Za-z_#@][A-Za-z0-9_@$#.-]*)";
let DecodeIdentifier = (token:string) {
    case(
        token startswith "[" and token endswith "]", replace_string(substring(token, 1, strlen(token) - 2), "]]", "]"),
        token startswith '"' and token endswith '"', replace_string(substring(token, 1, strlen(token) - 2), '""', '"'),
        token)
};
AzureDiagnostics
| where TimeGenerated >= ago(5m)
| where ResourceProvider =~ "MICROSOFT.SQL" and ResourceType =~ "MANAGEDINSTANCES"
| where Category == "SQLSecurityAuditEvents"
| extend ResourceId = coalesce(_ResourceId, ResourceId),
    ServerName = coalesce(server_instance_name_s, LogicalServerName_s),
    DatabaseName = database_name_s,
    Actor = coalesce(server_principal_name_s, session_server_principal_name_s),
    ClientIP = client_ip_s,
    ApplicationName = application_name_s,
    ClientHost = host_name_s,
    AuditAction = action_name_s,
    AuditSuccess = succeeded_s,
    Statement = statement_s,
    ConnectionId = tostring(connection_id_g),
    TargetAccount = coalesce(target_server_principal_name_s, target_database_principal_name_s),
    TargetRole = "",
    TargetObject = "",
    Details = additional_information_s
| extend IPAddress = iff(isnotnull(parse_ipv4(ClientIP)) or isnotempty(parse_ipv6(ClientIP)), ClientIP, "")
| where AuditSuccess =~ "true"
| extend ParsedRole = DecodeIdentifier(extract(strcat(@"(?i)\bALTER\s+ROLE\s+(", Identifier, @")\s+ADD\s+MEMBER\s+(", Identifier, ")"), 1, Statement)),
    ParsedMember = DecodeIdentifier(extract(strcat(@"(?i)\bALTER\s+ROLE\s+(", Identifier, @")\s+ADD\s+MEMBER\s+(", Identifier, ")"), 2, Statement))
| extend LegacyCall = extract(@"(?is)\bsp_addrolemember\s+(.+?)(?:;|$)", 1, Statement)
| extend LegacyFirst = extract(@"(?is)^\s*(?:@\w+\s*=\s*)?N?'((?:[^']|'')*)'", 1, LegacyCall),
    LegacySecond = extract(@"(?is)^\s*(?:@\w+\s*=\s*)?N?'(?:[^']|'')*'\s*,\s*(?:@\w+\s*=\s*)?N?'((?:[^']|'')*)'", 1, LegacyCall)
| extend LegacyRole = replace_string(LegacyFirst, "''", "'"),
    LegacyMember = replace_string(LegacySecond, "''", "'")
| extend TargetRole = coalesce(ParsedRole, LegacyRole),
    TargetAccount = coalesce(TargetAccount, ParsedMember, LegacyMember)
| where isnotempty(TargetRole)
| project TimeGenerated, ResourceId, ServerName, DatabaseName, Actor, ClientIP, IPAddress,
    ApplicationName, ClientHost, AuditAction, AuditSuccess, Statement, ConnectionId,
    TargetAccount, TargetRole, TargetObject, Details

properties.displayName: SQL MI - Multiple failed logins from one source IP
properties.description: More than five failures in ten minutes, grouped by MI resource and valid IPv4/IPv6 address. Missing or placeholder IP values cannot form an IP entity or trigger this rule. The actor list is context, not a claim that a single account was involved. Prerequisites: FAILED_LOGIN_GROUP with a valid client IP. Source: https://github.com/le0li9ht/Microsoft-Sentinel-Queries/blob/44de43909fee0564e2fb532bf09fe1c2cf4dd5ce/Azure%20SQL/MultipleFailedLoginsFromSingleIP.kql. All rules import disabled. Review audit coverage, source field quality, thresholds, and maintenance allowlists before enabling. Audit succeeded=true is a reported audit outcome, not independent verification that a transaction committed. Statement-based matching is heuristic and can miss dynamic SQL, comments between tokens, or multiple objects; inspect native audit context. Raw SQL may contain sensitive data; the query retains it for investigation but does not copy it into custom details.
properties.query:
let Identifier = @"(?:\[(?:[^\]]|\]\])+\]|\x22(?:[^\x22]|\x22\x22)+\x22|[A-Za-z_#@][A-Za-z0-9_@$#.-]*)";
let DecodeIdentifier = (token:string) {
    case(
        token startswith "[" and token endswith "]", replace_string(substring(token, 1, strlen(token) - 2), "]]", "]"),
        token startswith '"' and token endswith '"', replace_string(substring(token, 1, strlen(token) - 2), '""', '"'),
        token)
};
AzureDiagnostics
| where TimeGenerated >= ago(10m)
| where ResourceProvider =~ "MICROSOFT.SQL" and ResourceType =~ "MANAGEDINSTANCES"
| where Category == "SQLSecurityAuditEvents"
| extend ResourceId = coalesce(_ResourceId, ResourceId),
    ServerName = coalesce(server_instance_name_s, LogicalServerName_s),
    DatabaseName = database_name_s,
    Actor = coalesce(server_principal_name_s, session_server_principal_name_s),
    ClientIP = client_ip_s,
    ApplicationName = application_name_s,
    ClientHost = host_name_s,
    AuditAction = action_name_s,
    AuditSuccess = succeeded_s,
    Statement = statement_s,
    ConnectionId = tostring(connection_id_g),
    TargetAccount = coalesce(target_server_principal_name_s, target_database_principal_name_s),
    TargetRole = "",
    TargetObject = "",
    Details = additional_information_s
| extend IPAddress = iff(isnotnull(parse_ipv4(ClientIP)) or isnotempty(parse_ipv6(ClientIP)), ClientIP, "")
| where action_id_s == "LGIF" or AuditAction =~ "LOGIN FAILED"
| where not(Actor =~ "AzureSQLConnectivityChecker" and ipv4_is_private(ClientIP) == true)
| where isnotempty(IPAddress)
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), TimeGenerated = max(TimeGenerated), FailedCount = count(),
    Accounts = make_set_if(Actor, isnotempty(Actor), 20)
    by ResourceId, ServerName, ClientIP, IPAddress
| where FailedCount > 5
| extend Actor = "", DatabaseName = "", ApplicationName = "", ClientHost = "",
    AuditAction = "LOGIN FAILED", AuditSuccess = "false", Statement = "", ConnectionId = "",
    TargetAccount = "", TargetRole = "", TargetObject = "",
    Details = strcat("Failed logins: ", FailedCount, "; accounts: ", tostring(Accounts))
| project TimeGenerated, ResourceId, ServerName, DatabaseName, Actor, ClientIP, IPAddress,
    ApplicationName, ClientHost, AuditAction, AuditSuccess, Statement, ConnectionId,
    TargetAccount, TargetRole, TargetObject, Details, FirstSeen, FailedCount

Audit success is not independent proof of committed deletion; IF EXISTS can be a no-op. Prerequisites: SCHEMA_OBJECT_CHANGE_GROUP, or BATCH_COMPLETED_GROUP capturing the statement. Source: https://github.com/le0li9ht/Microsoft-Sentinel-Queries/blob/44de43909fee0564e2fb532bf09fe1c2cf4dd5ce/Azure%20SQL/TableDeletedSuccessfully.kql. All rules import disabled. Review audit coverage, source field quality, thresholds, and maintenance allowlists before enabling. Audit succeeded=true is a reported audit outcome, not independent verification that a transaction committed. Statement-based matching is heuristic and can miss dynamic SQL, comments between tokens, or multiple objects; inspect native audit context. Raw SQL may contain sensitive data; the query retains it for investigation but does not copy it into custom details.
properties.query:
let Identifier = @"(?:\[(?:[^\]]|\]\])+\]|\x22(?:[^\x22]|\x22\x22)+\x22|[A-Za-z_#@][A-Za-z0-9_@$#.-]*)";
let DecodeIdentifier = (token:string) {
    case(
        token startswith "[" and token endswith "]", replace_string(substring(token, 1, strlen(token) - 2), "]]", "]"),
        token startswith '"' and token endswith '"', replace_string(substring(token, 1, strlen(token) - 2), '""', '"'),
        token)
};
AzureDiagnostics
| where TimeGenerated >= ago(5m)
| where ResourceProvider =~ "MICROSOFT.SQL" and ResourceType =~ "MANAGEDINSTANCES"
| where Category == "SQLSecurityAuditEvents"
| extend ResourceId = coalesce(_ResourceId, ResourceId),
    ServerName = coalesce(server_instance_name_s, LogicalServerName_s),
    DatabaseName = database_name_s,
    Actor = coalesce(server_principal_name_s, session_server_principal_name_s),
    ClientIP = client_ip_s,
    ApplicationName = application_name_s,
    ClientHost = host_name_s,
    AuditAction = action_name_s,
    AuditSuccess = succeeded_s,
    Statement = statement_s,
    ConnectionId = tostring(connection_id_g),
    TargetAccount = coalesce(target_server_principal_name_s, target_database_principal_name_s),
    TargetRole = "",
    TargetObject = "",
    Details = additional_information_s
| extend IPAddress = iff(isnotnull(parse_ipv4(ClientIP)) or isnotempty(parse_ipv6(ClientIP)), ClientIP, "")
| where AuditSuccess =~ "true"
| extend TargetObject = extract(strcat(@"(?i)\bDROP\s+TABLE\s+(?:IF\s+EXISTS\s+)?(", Identifier, @"(?:\s*\.\s*", Identifier, "){0,2})"), 1, Statement)
